# Fagus sylvatica
| _Fagus sylvatica_ |
|-|
| [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Fagus-sylvatica-cansiglio-forest-italy.jpg/500px-Fagus-sylvatica-cansiglio-forest-italy.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fagus-sylvatica-cansiglio-forest-italy.jpg) |
| [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/Fagus_sylvatica_range.svg/500px-Fagus_sylvatica_range.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fagus_sylvatica_range.svg) |

_**Fagus sylvatica**_, the **European beech** or **common beech**, is a large [deciduous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deciduous) tree in the [beech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagaceae) family with smooth silvery-grey bark, large leaf area, and a short trunk with low branches.

## Description
_Fagus sylvatica_ is a large [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree), capable of reaching heights of up to 50 metres (160 feet) tall[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_sylvatica#cite_note-4) and 3m (10ft) trunk diameter, though more typically 25–35m (82–115ft) tall and up to 1.5m (5ft) trunk diameter. A 10-year-old sapling will stand about 4m (13ft) tall. Like most trees, its form depends on the location; in forest areas, _F.sylvatica_ grows to over 30m (98ft), with branches being high up on the trunk.

The [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaves) are alternate, simple, and entire or with a slightly [crenate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crenate) margin, 5–10cm (2–3+7⁄8in) long and 3–7cm (1.2–2.8in) broad, with 6–7 veins on each side of the leaf (as opposed to 7–10 veins in _[F.orientalis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_orientalis)_).
